{{ElectionsIA}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in Iowa''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Iowa]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congresswoman [[Ashley Hinson]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state representative [[Josh Turek]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent [[Joni Ernst]] is not seeking a third term.<ref name="ErnstRetire"/>

[[Primary elections]] were held on June 2. Endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], Hinson won the Republican nomination with 73.9% of the vote over former state senator [[Jim Carlin (politician)|Jim Carlin]]. Turek won the Democratic nomination with 62.6% of the vote over state senator [[Zach Wahls]].

Democrats have not won a Senate election in Iowa since [[2008 United States Senate election in Iowa|2008]]. This is Iowa's first open Senate election to be held concurrently with an [[2026 Iowa gubernatorial election|open gubernatorial election]] since [[1968 United States Senate election in Iowa|1968]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Could Iowa Democrats Win 2026's Gubernatorial and US Senate Races? |url=https://smartpolitics.lib.umn.edu/2026/06/03/could-iowa-democrats-win-2026s-gubernatorial-and-us-senate-races/ |work=Smart Politics |date=June 3, 2026 |accessdate=June 6, 2026}}</ref>

== Background ==
Since voting for President [[Barack Obama]] in both [[2008 United States presidential election in Iowa|2008]] and [[2012 United States presidential election in Iowa|2012]], Iowa has trended increasingly Republican and is now considered a moderately to strongly [[red state]] at the federal and state level. Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] won Iowa in [[2020 United States presidential election in Iowa|2020]] by 8 percentage points, and in [[2024 United States presidential election in Iowa|2024]] grew his margin to 13 percentage points. Republicans control every statewide executive office (except the [[Iowa Auditor of State|state auditor's office]]), majorities in both chambers of the [[Iowa State Legislature|state legislature]], and the entire congressional delegation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ta |first=Linh |date=2024-11-06 |title=Iowa remains solidly Republican |url=https://www.axios.com/local/des-moines/2024/11/06/iowa-remains-red-despite-iowa-poll-republicans |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |language=en}}</ref>  Incumbent Senator Joni Ernst was [[2014 United States Senate election in Iowa|first elected]] as part of the [[2014 United States Senate elections|2014]] [[Wave elections in the United States|red wave]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barrett |first=Ted |date=2014-11-05 |title=Joni Ernst wins Iowa Senate race |url=https://www.cnn.com/2014/11/05/politics/iowa-senate-digital/index.html |access-date=2024-12-13 |website=[[CNN]] |language=en}}</ref> and was reelected in [[2020 United States Senate election in Iowa|2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pfannenstiel |first=Brianne |title='Six more years!': Republican U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst wins reelection, beating Democrat Theresa Greenfield |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/news/politics/2020/11/02/iowa-election-results-us-senate-theresa-greenfield-joni-ernst/5997461002/ |access-date=December 13, 2024 |date=November 2, 2020 |website=[[The Des Moines Register]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

In the latter half of her second term, Ernst came under increasing pressure.  In December 2024, she faced pushback from Republicans for her skepticism of [[Pete Hegseth]]'s nomination for [[United States Secretary of Defense|Secretary of Defense]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Copp |first1=Tara |title=Sen. Joni Ernst wants to hear from Hegseth on sex assault in the military and women in combat |url=https://apnews.com/article/ernst-hegseth-nominee-trump-vetting-assault-pentagon-138c79c9199c8525d43b77417674d81e |access-date=17 October 2026 |agency=Associated Press |date=December 7th 2024}}</ref>  She later sparked controversy for replying "we are all going to die" when a constituent confronted her for deaths that could be caused by cuts to [[Medicaid]] and [[Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program|SNAP]], which she supported as part of the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSN |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/were-all-going-to-die-gop-fumbles-defense-of-medicaid-cuts/ar-AA1FXvi2 |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=www.msn.com}}</ref> 

In September 2025, Ernst announced that she would not seek reelection, officially citing family obligations, although her decision was interpreted in light of previous controversies.  The resulting open seat was expected to make the race more competitive.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Opsahl |first1=Robin |title=U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst announces she will not seek reelection |url=https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2025/09/02/u-s-sen-joni-ernst-announces-she-will-not-seek-reelection/ |access-date=17 October 2026 |work=Iowa Capital Dispatch |agency=Iowa Capital Dispatch |date=2 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=The Associated Press |title=Sen. Joni Ernst of Iowa confirms she will not run for reelection in 2026 |url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2025/09/02/sen-joni-ernst-of-iowa-confirms-she-will-not-run-for-reelection-in-2026 |website=MPR News |access-date=17 October 2026 |language=en |date=2 September 2025}}</ref>

== Libertarian primary ==
On June 2, the Laehn campaign submitted nearly 10,000 signatures to the Iowa Secretary of State, satisfying the 3,500 signature requirement to qualify for the ballot.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Laehn Submits Nomination Petitions to Qualify for 2026 U.S. Senate Race - The Iowa Standard | url=https://theiowastandard.com/laehn-submits-nomination-petitions-to-qualify-for-2026-u-s-senate-race/ | access-date=2026-08-02 | website=theiowastandard.com | date=June 2, 2026 }}</ref> Laehn was added to the candidate list as the Libertarian Party's candidate.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://sos.iowa.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/2026%20General%20-%20Candidate%20List%20Database%20-%20All%20Elections.pdf | title=Candidate List - November 3, 2026 General Election | website=sos.iowa.gov}}</ref>
